title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location telemetry by the wearer
description: By wearing the device continuously, the user discloses raw sensor telemetry including heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps to the wearable. These data reveal intimate facts about health status, routines, whereabouts, and daily habits.
assumptions: Assumes the wearable receives and can access the raw telemetry generated during use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Linkability of telemetry records over time
description: Continuous transmission of heart rate, activity, GPS position, and timestamps can allow records from different moments to be linked to the same wearer, enabling reconstruction of routines, trips, and behavior patterns even if explicit identifiers are absent.
assumptions: Assumes repeated observations on this flow are associated through stable device, timing, or signal patterns.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ; this is a best-fit linkability node.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from location and biometric patterns
description: GPS traces, timestamps, and physiological/activity patterns can identify the wearer directly or indirectly. Home/work locations, unique movement habits, or distinctive biometric signatures may single out the individual even without a name on the flow.
assumptions: Assumes an observer or recipient can correlate telemetry with external knowledge or datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific.

title: Inference of sensitive attributes by the wearable device
description: Once received, the wearable can process the telemetry to infer additional sensitive information such as health conditions, exercise intensity, sleep/wake cycles, religious attendance, workplace, home address, or other lifestyle attributes beyond the raw data itself.
assumptions: Assumes the device software performs or enables analytics over the incoming telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for disclosure via derived/inferred data.

title: Unawareness of continuous collection scope
description: The wearer may be insufficiently aware that the device continuously captures multiple sensor streams, including precise location and timestamps, and of the privacy implications of such persistent monitoring.
assumptions: Assumes notices, UI cues, or onboarding do not fully convey the extent and sensitivity of collection.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ; chosen as best-fit unawareness node.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive or unjustified collection
description: Continuous collection of heart rate, steps, GPS position, and timestamps may exceed what is necessary for a given function if all streams are always captured by default, creating risk of violating data minimization, purpose limitation, or consent requirements.
assumptions: Assumes some product features may not require all listed data at all times or at the stated granularity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact compliance subtree may differ.

title: Repudiation gaps around telemetry collection consent or initiation
description: If the wearable does not maintain clear evidence of when telemetry collection started, what sensors were enabled, and what the wearer agreed to, disputes may arise about whether collection was authorized or expected.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on consent or user configuration and lacks robust auditability.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability is somewhat context-dependent for this flow; included as a possible threat rather than certain.

title: Stable device identifier enables linking of sessions and traces
description: The wearable shares a persistent device id together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. This allows records from multiple syncs to be linked to the same person or device over time, building a longitudinal activity profile.
assumptions: The device id is stable across sync events and visible to the app.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Data in transit can identify the user through GPS traces and device id
description: The flow contains direct or quasi-identifiers such as device id, precise GPS traces, and timestamps. If observed in transit, these can identify or single out the user.
assumptions: An attacker or unintended party can observe the sync traffic or exposed metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Communication metadata can link wearable and app interactions
description: Even aside from payload contents, repeated sync timing, endpoints, and transfer patterns may allow linking a specific wearable to a specific mobile app instance and correlating activity over time.
assumptions: Observable transport or network metadata exists during sync.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Companion app can infer sensitive habits and locations from received data
description: By receiving exercise sessions, precise GPS traces, and timestamps, the app can derive home/work locations, routines, health-related patterns, and other sensitive behavioral inferences beyond the raw data itself.
assumptions: The app stores or analyzes the synced history.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Companion app may process more data than necessary for synchronization
description: The app receives full sensor batches including precise GPS traces, timestamps, and device id, which may exceed what is necessary for basic syncing or user feedback, creating a data minimization risk.
assumptions: Some app functions could operate with reduced precision, fewer fields, or less retention.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Users may be unaware of the extent of synced telemetry
description: The companion app may not make it sufficiently clear that detailed exercise sessions, precise GPS traces, timestamps, and a stable device identifier are synced and potentially retained or analyzed, undermining user awareness and control.
assumptions: Not all synced fields and downstream uses are transparently communicated to the user.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Sync may occur without valid or sufficiently specific consent/legal basis
description: If the app collects and processes detailed location and activity history by default, without granular opt-in or another appropriate legal basis, the receipt and processing of this data may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Precise location and activity data require explicit consent or similarly strong justification in the deployment context.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on jurisdiction and product context; node id is best-effort.

title: User may be unable to prove or contest what data was synced
description: If the app does not provide reliable records or receipts of synchronization events and payload categories, the user may be unable to demonstrate what data was transmitted, when, and under which settings, weakening accountability and contestability.
assumptions: The system lacks user-accessible audit trails for sync operations.
uncertainty_note: This is a weaker fit than other threats for this flow; node id is best-effort.

title: Direct identification through highly personal health and diet entries
description: By manually entering calorie intake, meals, and weight, the wearer shares data that can directly identify or single them out when combined with account context in the app. Weight logs and detailed meal patterns are strongly personal and may reveal the identity of the wearer to the receiving system or anyone with access to it.
assumptions: The app account or device context can be tied to a specific individual.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for direct identification may vary.

title: Linkability of diet and weight records over time
description: Repeated manual entries about meals, calories, and weight can be linked together over time to build a longitudinal profile of the same wearer. This enables correlation of habits, routines, and health-related behavior across sessions.
assumptions: The app stores entries under a persistent account, device identifier, or stable pseudonym.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability across records may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and lifestyle information by submission
description: The act of submitting calorie intake, meals, and weight discloses sensitive personal information about health status, eating habits, and lifestyle to the app. Such data may expose dieting behavior, possible medical conditions, or other intimate facts.
assumptions: Weight and dietary logs are treated as sensitive personal data in the system context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort; exact disclosure subtree may vary.

title: Linkability via transmission metadata
description: Even if the content is protected, metadata on this flow such as timing, frequency, device/app identifiers, and network characteristics can allow repeated submissions to be linked to the same wearer or household.
assumptions: Transmission or application-layer metadata is observable to the app backend, platform provider, or network intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to a metadata-based linkability node.

title: Identifiability from flow metadata
description: Metadata associated with the submission flow, such as device identifiers, IP address, account tokens, or mobile advertising identifiers, may identify the wearer even without inspecting the meal or weight content itself.
assumptions: The mobile app or supporting infrastructure attaches persistent identifiers to requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to an identifiability-through-metadata node.

title: Excessive disclosure through storage and further processing in the app
description: Upon receipt, the companion app may store, analyze, or repurpose detailed food and weight entries beyond what is necessary for immediate logging, increasing exposure of sensitive health and behavioral information.
assumptions: The app persists entries locally or remotely and may use them for analytics, personalization, or sharing with other components.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to a destination-side disclosure node.

title: Unawareness of downstream use of nutrition and weight data
description: The wearer may not be fully aware of how the companion app uses, stores, combines, or shares manually logged calorie, meal, and weight data after receipt. This creates a risk that processing occurs without meaningful user understanding.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-app explanations may be incomplete, hard to find, or too vague.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort; exact unawareness subtree may differ.

title: Processing of sensitive diet and weight data beyond user expectations or valid consent
description: The app may process manually logged nutrition and weight data for secondary purposes, such as profiling, analytics, or sharing with partners, without a sufficiently specific legal basis or consent aligned with the user's expectations.
assumptions: The app ecosystem includes secondary processing or sharing beyond core calorie/weight tracking.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to a non-compliance/invalid-consent node.

title: Repudiation of submitted entries or consent context
description: If the app does not preserve adequate context around manual submissions, the wearer may later dispute having entered certain meals or weight values, or the app operator may be unable to demonstrate what was submitted and under what notice/consent conditions. This can create privacy-relevant accountability issues.
assumptions: Submission events and associated notice/consent context are not robustly logged or attributable.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is somewhat uncertain because non-repudiation is often less central for this kind of user-to-app logging flow; node id is best-effort.

title: Excessive disclosure of sensitive health data by the app
description: The mobile app may write more health-log detail than is necessary for the intended service purpose, such as granular calorie intake, full weight history, and detailed exercise sessions, increasing exposure of sensitive health information.
assumptions: Assumes some service functions could be fulfilled with less granular or less frequent data than what is written to the store.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on disclosure via oversharing/minimisation failure; exact LINDDUN Pro node label may vary.

title: Linkability via persistent identifiers and repeated health-log uploads
description: Repeated writes from the same app instance to the health log store can be linked together through stable account identifiers, device identifiers, session tokens, or consistent metadata, enabling construction of a longitudinal profile of the user's health behavior.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries or is accompanied by stable identifiers or metadata that persist across uploads.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability from repeated observations of the same flow.

title: Identifiability from health-log content or metadata in transit
description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, the combination of weight history, exercise patterns, timestamps, and associated metadata may uniquely identify a user or make them distinguishable within a population.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted records contain quasi-identifiers or are associated with account/device metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from data content/metadata; exact subtree may differ.

title: Disclosure through insecure storage or overly broad access at the health log store
description: Once received, the health log store may expose sensitive health logs to unauthorized internal components, administrators, analytics jobs, or attackers if access controls, segregation, or encryption at rest are insufficient.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore persists the logs and may be accessible by multiple services or operators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure caused by storage/recipient-side access control weaknesses.

title: Linkability of multiple health events within the datastore
description: The datastore can correlate calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions over time under the same user record, enabling detailed linkage across contexts and periods beyond what the user may expect.
assumptions: Assumes records are stored under a common account or other persistent key.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side linking of records over time.

title: Identification of the user from stored health histories
description: The accumulated health-log history in the store may allow the organization or anyone with access to infer the identity of a person from distinctive patterns, especially when combined with account data or other datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore is logically or practically linkable to account or profile information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side identification through combination with stored data.

title: Unawareness of long-term storage and secondary use of health logs
description: Users may not realize that detailed health logs are retained, analyzed, or reused for purposes such as personalization, analytics, or model improvement after being written to the store.
assumptions: Assumes notices are incomplete, unclear, or not presented at the time of collection/storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency at the recipient.

title: Non-compliance with data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations
description: Storing detailed calorie, weight, and exercise histories without clear necessity, lawful basis, retention limits, or adequate safeguards may violate privacy or health-data protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the data qualifies as sensitive health-related data under applicable law or policy and that governance controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for compliance failures related to sensitive-data storage and retention.

title: Detectability of a user's engagement in health tracking
description: The mere presence of records in the health log store, or observable write events to it, may reveal that a particular user is using health-tracking features or has ongoing health-management activity, even without exposing full content.
assumptions: Assumes some party can observe datastore events, record existence, or traffic patterns associated with this flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of participation/activity from record existence or write patterns.

title: Excessive collection of precise location traces
description: The mobile app writes detailed GPS traces with timestamps to persistent storage, enabling collection of more precise and frequent location data than is necessary for the stated purpose. This creates a privacy threat because highly granular location histories can reveal habits, home/work locations, and sensitive visits.
assumptions: Assumes the app may collect/store continuous or high-frequency GPS traces rather than coarse or minimized location data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for detectability/disclosure-related overcollection may differ.

title: Linkability through persistent device or account association in location-write events
description: Each write of timestamped GPS traces from the app to the location history store can be associated with the same user, device, or account over time. This enables linking multiple records together into a longitudinal movement profile, even if direct identifiers are minimized.
assumptions: Assumes records carry a stable pseudonym, account id, device id, session token, or are otherwise attributable to the same subject across writes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers/record correlation.

title: Identifiability from precise spatiotemporal traces in transit
description: Precise GPS coordinates combined with timestamps are often sufficient to identify an individual by inference, for example by locating a home address, workplace, or unique travel pattern. The data flow itself therefore carries identifying information even without explicit names.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted traces are precise enough and frequent enough to support singling out or re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for identifiability due to quasi-identifiers/inference.

title: Disclosure of sensitive activities from stored location history
description: Once received and stored, the location history store can reveal sensitive information such as visits to clinics, places of worship, political events, or other intimate routines. Processing or querying the stored traces may disclose far more about the user than the raw purpose of storage suggests.
assumptions: Assumes the store retains historical traces and supports later access, analysis, or sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for information disclosure/inference from stored personal data.

title: Unawareness of retention and secondary use of location history
description: Users may be unaware that their detailed location traces are retained in a history store, for how long they are kept, and whether they are later used for analytics, profiling, or sharing. This lack of transparency undermines informed expectations about the processing.
assumptions: Assumes retention periods, downstream uses, or visibility controls are not clearly communicated in the app experience.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for insufficient transparency/unawareness.

title: Non-compliance risk from storing location history without valid legal basis or minimization
description: Persistently storing timestamped GPS traces may violate privacy requirements if the system lacks valid consent or another legal basis, retains data longer than necessary, or fails to implement data minimization and purpose limitation for sensitive location data.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy law or policy imposes requirements on lawful basis, minimization, retention, and purpose limitation.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ; this is a best-fit non-compliance classification from memory.

title: Cross-session health logs enable linkage of records to the same individual
description: The store discloses calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions to the analytics service, allowing records from multiple sessions to be linked together as belonging to the same person or household profile.
assumptions: The analytics service receives a stable account, device, or record identifier, or otherwise enough consistency in the data to correlate sessions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via shared identifiers/correlatable records.

title: Health-condition analysis may identify the individual behind the logs
description: By analyzing longitudinal calorie, weight, and exercise patterns, the analytics service may be able to identify a specific person directly or single them out from a small group, especially when combined with existing account context.
assumptions: P3 has access to account context, device context, or auxiliary data that can connect the logs to a natural person.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability/singling out at the recipient; exact subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Inference of sensitive health conditions from longitudinal logs
description: The analytics service can derive sensitive information, such as obesity trends, eating disorders, mobility limitations, pregnancy-related changes, or other health conditions, from repeated calorie, weight, and exercise entries over time.
assumptions: P3 performs profiling or statistical analysis over historical logs rather than only transient computation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure by inference/derivation; exact node label may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Analytics service may process more historical health data than necessary
description: Reading calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions for analysis may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose if full history, fine granularity, or unrelated attributes are ingested instead of minimized or aggregated data.
assumptions: The analysis could be performed with less data, shorter retention windows, or aggregated features.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization / excessive collection or use at the destination.

title: Secondary analytics use of health logs may be insufficiently transparent
description: Individuals may not understand that their detailed health logs are read across sessions for health-condition analysis, especially if the processing goes beyond core logging functionality or includes profiling.
assumptions: Notices or in-product explanations do not clearly describe this longitudinal analysis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node may differ by threat-tree edition.

title: Health-condition analysis may occur without valid consent or another appropriate legal basis
description: Because calorie, weight, and exercise logs can reveal special-category health information, using them for health-condition analysis may require explicit consent or another specific legal basis; absent that, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats these logs or derived conditions as sensitive health data and requires heightened justification.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of lawful basis/consent; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Cross-session linkage of location records to build a persistent mobility profile
description: The analytics service queries location history across sessions and combines records over time, enabling linkage of multiple observations to the same individual or device and construction of a persistent movement profile.
assumptions: Location history records are associated with a stable account, device, pseudonym, or other recurring identifier that allows cross-session correlation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability via correlation across contexts/sessions; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may vary.

title: Identification of an individual from unique movement patterns
description: Daily routine and movement patterns derived from historical location traces can uniquely distinguish a person, allowing the analytics service to identify or single out the data subject even if raw records were initially pseudonymous.
assumptions: Mobility traces contain sufficiently granular spatiotemporal points or are combined with auxiliary knowledge such as home/work locations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from quasi-identifying behavioral/location data; numbering may be approximate.

description: By analyzing location history across sessions, the service can infer private facts such as home address, workplace, religious attendance, medical visits, political activity, relationships, and other sensitive behavioral patterns beyond the original collection context.
assumptions: The service has access to sufficiently detailed historical location data and points of interest or other enrichment sources.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure through inference/analysis of received data; exact node id may differ in your threat tree version.

title: Secondary use of location history for behavioral analytics beyond user expectations
description: Location history collected over sessions is used to derive daily routine and movement patterns, which may exceed the purpose expected by the user or originally communicated when the data was collected.
assumptions: The original purpose of storing location history did not clearly include long-term behavioral profiling for analytics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for use of data beyond expected/declared purpose; numbering may be approximate.

title: Insufficient transparency or legal basis for long-term mobility profiling
description: If users were not adequately informed, did not consent where required, or cannot exercise applicable rights regarding analysis of historical location data, the destination processing may violate data protection obligations for purpose limitation, transparency, or lawful basis.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulation requires notice, lawful basis, and potentially consent or opt-out for this profiling activity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance arising from analytics/profiling without adequate notice or lawful basis; exact node id may vary.

title: Exposure of sensitive location history in transit
description: The flow carries historical location data whose contents reveal movement patterns; if the transmission is observable or insufficiently protected, sensitive whereabouts and routines could be disclosed during transfer from the store to the analytics service.
assumptions: Transport protections may be absent, weak, or terminable by intermediaries with access to plaintext.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of data in transit; exact numbering may differ.

title: Sharing inferred health-risk indicators can identify or single out the user
description: The analytics service sends highly specific inferred insights such as health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags to the mobile app. Even if direct identifiers are absent from the payload, the sensitivity and uniqueness of these inferences can enable identification or singling out of the data subject by the receiving context or anyone with access to the app.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability via disclosure of sensitive inferred attributes; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may vary.

title: Disclosure of sensitive inferred health information to the app
description: The source process discloses inferred health-related insights to the companion app. These insights may reveal sensitive medical conditions, behavioral patterns, or elevated risks beyond what the user expects, increasing privacy harm if exposed within the app ecosystem.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for disclosure of personal/sensitive data by sharing it with a recipient.

title: Flow contents and metadata can link analytics results to a specific user/device
description: The transmission of inferred insights from the analytics service to the mobile app may include stable account, device, session, or routing metadata. Combined with the distinctive nature of the returned insights, this can allow linking multiple messages and associating them with the same individual over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability through data-flow metadata and repeated transmissions.

title: Interception of inferred insights in transit
description: If the flow is insufficiently protected in transit, an attacker observing network traffic could learn sensitive inferred health-condition risks, routine summaries, or trend flags. This creates a disclosure threat on the data flow itself.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure during transmission; exact numbering may differ.

title: App may use inferred insights in ways unexpected by the user
description: On receipt, the mobile app may present, combine, or further use inferred health insights for profiling, nudging, personalization, or onward sharing in ways the user does not anticipate. This creates a threat that the data is processed beyond the user's expectations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unexpected secondary use at the destination.

title: Local storage or display in the app can expose sensitive inferences
description: The destination app may cache, log, persist, or prominently display the returned insights on the device. Other apps, device users, notifications, screenshots, backups, or compromised endpoints could then access sensitive inferred health information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure caused by recipient-side storage/display.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for receiving inferred health insights
description: The app may receive and process inferred health-condition risk indicators and trend flags without adequately informing the user or obtaining appropriate consent for this category of sensitive inferred data. This can undermine compliance with consent and transparency obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to inadequate consent/transparency; exact numbering may vary.

title: Disclosure of sensitive inferred health indicators to an unintended viewer via the app dashboard
description: The mobile app presents highly sensitive inferred condition indicators and trends (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals). If the dashboard is shown when someone else can observe the screen, or if the app exposes the information without adequate access control or session protection, the act of displaying it can disclose special-category health information to unintended parties.
assumptions: Assumes the app may be viewed in shared physical environments or may lack strong re-authentication before showing sensitive insights.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is my best-fit estimate for disclosure through information presentation/access control at the source; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: User may be unaware that the dashboard reveals inferred health-risk conclusions
description: The app may show risk signals and trend-based condition indicators without making clear how these inferences were derived, how sensitive they are, or what their implications are. This can leave the wearer insufficiently informed about the privacy impact of receiving and potentially exposing these inferences.
assumptions: Assumes explanations, just-in-time notices, or sensitivity cues may be limited or absent in the UI.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node for insufficient user awareness around privacy-relevant inference display; exact node id may differ.

title: Presentation of inferred condition indicators may exceed or conflict with the user's consent expectations
description: Displaying eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals may go beyond what the user reasonably expected when using the companion app, especially if they consented to wellness tracking but not to sensitive health inference generation and presentation. The privacy threat arises when the app shares these inferences with the user without consent that is specific and informed for this purpose.
assumptions: Assumes consent may have been broad, bundled, or not specific to sensitive inference generation and display.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for non-compliance/consent-specificity issues in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Interception of dashboard content in transit could identify the wearer as having specific health risks
description: If the dashboard data is transmitted over a network or inter-process channel without sufficient protection, an attacker observing the flow could identify the user and learn that the content concerns eating-disorder or diabetes risk indicators. Even metadata or payload fragments may reveal the user's association with sensitive health conditions.
assumptions: Assumes this flow involves electronic transmission between app components or backend-mediated delivery rather than purely local rendering.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if DF9 includes data in transit over a channel that can be observed; if this is purely local display, this threat may not apply. Node id is approximate.

title: Sensitive health inferences could be disclosed through insecure transmission
description: The inferred condition indicators and trends are sensitive health-related data. If the flow is not adequately protected in transit, the content could be exposed to eavesdroppers, revealing intimate information about the wearer.
assumptions: Assumes network or IPC transmission occurs and transport/channel protections may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: If the flow is only a conceptual app-to-user display with no interceptable transmission, this may be less applicable. Tree node is best-fit approximate.

title: Recipient-side onward disclosure by the user or their device environment
description: Once the wearer receives the dashboard output, the information may be exposed onward through screenshots, screen recording, notification mirroring, shared-device features, or observation by others nearby. The privacy threat arises at the destination because the received sensitive inferences can be further disclosed in the recipient's environment.
assumptions: Assumes the user's device or surroundings may permit onward exposure after receipt.

description: The analytics service shares the full health and location dataset, along with models and analytics data, with a third-party cloud provider for hosting and replication. Sending the full dataset may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the hosting purpose, especially highly sensitive health and precise location data.

title: Cloud provider can link health and location records across datasets and tenants
description: Upon receiving hosted analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset, the cloud provider may be able to link records belonging to the same individual across backups, replicas, logs, and related hosted datasets. assumptions: Assumes the provider has technical access to stored content or metadata sufficient to correlate records across storage objects, replicas, or services.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best estimate for linkability at the destination; exact node numbering may differ.

title: Cloud provider can identify individuals from hosted health and location data
description: The full dataset contains health and location information that can directly or indirectly identify individuals. Even if direct identifiers are absent, combinations of health attributes, movement patterns, and location traces may enable re-identification by the cloud provider.
assumptions: Assumes the dataset is not fully anonymized and that the provider can access plaintext data or sufficiently rich derived artifacts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability/re-identification at the recipient.

title: Transfer metadata may reveal linkage between analytics service and hosted health dataset
description: Metadata of the transfer itself, such as endpoints, timing, volume, replication patterns, and storage destinations, may allow observers or the provider to infer that a particular health analytics service is associated with a specific sensitive dataset or customer population. This can create linkability even beyond the payload contents.
assumptions: Assumes transfer or replication metadata is observable to the cloud provider and/or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for linkability via communication metadata.

title: Transfer metadata may reveal the existence of identifiable sensitive processing
description: Even without inspecting payload contents, data-flow metadata such as large recurring uploads, region-specific replication, or naming conventions may reveal that identifiable health and location data about individuals is being processed and hosted.
assumptions: Assumes metadata is exposed in transit or to the receiving provider through operational telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for identifiability/inference from flow metadata.

title: Secondary use or over-retention of hosted dataset by cloud provider
description: After receipt, the cloud provider may retain replicas, backups, snapshots, or logs longer than expected, or use the hosted data for operational analytics, service improvement, or other secondary purposes. This constitutes disclosure beyond the original expectations of the data subjects and controller.
assumptions: Assumes contractual/technical controls do not fully prevent provider-side retention or secondary processing.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their full health and location data is hosted by a third-party cloud provider
description: Individuals may not realize that their sensitive health and location data, analytics outputs, and models are stored and replicated with an external cloud provider. This lack of awareness reduces transparency about who processes the data and where it resides.
assumptions: Assumes notices are incomplete, unclear, or do not specifically mention third-party cloud hosting/replication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness/lack of transparency.

title: Third-party cloud hosting and replication may be incompatible with stated purpose, consent, or data-handling commitments
description: Hosting and replicating the full health and location dataset at an external provider may conflict with consent terms, purpose limitation, data residency commitments, or contractual restrictions, especially given the sensitivity of health and location data.
assumptions: Assumes there are legal, policy, consent, or contractual constraints on outsourcing, cross-border replication, or processing of sensitive data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance; exact node numbering may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of provider-side handling may hinder accountability for hosting and replication actions
description: If the cloud provider's receipt, replication, access, deletion, or restoration actions are not logged or auditable in a privacy-preserving and trustworthy way, the parties may later be unable to prove what happened to the sensitive dataset. This weakens accountability and can enable repudiation of privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Assumes audit trails, attestations, or contractual reporting from the provider are incomplete or disputed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation/accountability issues at destination.
